title: Automated compliance batch deliveries with verifiable manifests
creator: Aisha Patel
summary: Build a tenant-scoped, region-aware scheduled export service that produces signed PDF/CSV bundles with an auditable manifest and dashboard for monitoring and delivery status.
body:
Background: Customers in regulated industries have requested an easy, auditable way to receive periodic exports of compliance evidence and usage ledgers (PDF and CSV outputs) that respect data residency and retention policies. Current manual exports are ad-hoc, error-prone, and lack tamper-evident manifests or a unified delivery schedule.

Goal: Ship a managed scheduled-export capability that: (1) generates per-tenant, residency-aware export bundles in PDF and CSV, (2) attaches a verifiable manifest (checksums + cryptographic signature) for audit, (3) supports configurable delivery channels (S3 with region routing, SFTP, and signed download URLs), and (4) surfaces export health, run history, and retention controls in the Console.

Scope (MVP):
- Export formats: CSV (canonical tabular ledger) and PDF (human-readable evidence summary).
- Scheduling: daily / weekly / monthly cron presets and ad-hoc manual runs.
- Delivery targets: region-scoped S3 buckets (preferred), fallback to encrypted SFTP endpoint.
- Manifest: package-level manifest containing file list, SHA256 checksums, file sizes, time window covered, residency tag, and a signing token. Signing implemented via KMS/HSM-backed RSA signature (integration ticket ENG-5317).
- Tenant scoping & residency: exports include only tenant-authorized records and are routed to destination endpoints filtered by residency policy.
- Retention: exported bundles tied to tenant retention settings; Console exposes auto-delete TTL for delivered bundles.
- Observability: Console widget for scheduled exports (status, last run, last size, failures), telemetry events for run start/finish/failure, and alerting for repeated failures.

Non-goals: incremental streaming exports, ad-hoc per-record redaction engine (redaction limited to configurable field set in this MVP), exports to arbitrary third-party SaaS (out of scope for initial release).

Design & UX notes: Console will provide a new "Exports" section under Compliance for each tenant workspace. UX components: schedule form (cron presets + custom CRON), destinations config (S3 region selector + key prefix), retention policy selector (days/weeks/months), and run-history table with downloadable signed manifests and file links. Design ticket DES-221 will produce mocks and accessibility checklist.

Operational design: Exports processed by a dedicated "export-worker" queue (ENG-5021). Workers will run data extraction in-residency (where possible) to avoid cross-region transfers, produce finalized bundle in a staging bucket, run checksum/signing, and atomically move to destination or push via SFTP. Backoff policy: exponential backoff with jitter; retry budget limited to 5 attempts before marking export as failed and opening an incident.

Security & compliance: Bundles are encrypted-at-rest in staging, delivered encrypted (SSE-S3 or client-managed KMS), and manifests are signed via customer/tenant-scoped key material stored in KMS. Access to export download links is short-lived and bound to auditable tokens. Security review required prior to release.

Telemetry & success metrics:
- Primary: percent of scheduled exports successfully delivered within SLA (target 99.5% after GA).
- Secondary: time from schedule trigger to delivery, average bytes per export, number of manual retries per tenant, number of security exceptions.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field for machine-checkable items.

Rollout plan:
1) Internal alpha with infra + security teams (2 weeks) to validate KMS signing and S3 residency routing.
2) Closed beta with 3 enterprise customers (4 weeks) to validate file formats, delivery plumbing, and retention behaviors.
3) GA release with feature flag and migration guide for tenants who want archived deliveries enabled (target GA in next minor release).

Notes / edge cases:
- When tenant retention is less than export window, export should fail-fast and notify tenant to adjust policy or choose a shorter window.
- If destination lacks required residency (e.g., S3 bucket in different region), system must either reject the schedule at validation time or apply an approved fallback per tenant policy (documented in Console).
- Large tenants: support chunking of bundles by size and manifest contains multiple parts.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Admin can create a scheduled export with format=CSV or PDF, a time window, destination, and retention TTL.
AC2: System produces a bundle that includes files, SHA256 checksums, total size, time window, residency tag, and a KMS-backed signature in the manifest.
AC3: Delivered bundle to S3 shows correct residency tag and retains object-level encryption (SSE-KMS or SSE-S3).
AC4: Console shows schedule status, last run timestamp, success/failure count, and provides links to download bundle and manifest (signed).
AC5: Retry behavior and failure states are observable; repeated failures generate an alert and a created internal incident ticket.
AC6: Export respects tenant retention settings; stored delivered bundles are auto-deleted after configured TTL.
